title: How Contagious Yawning Works
summary: Hosts Josh Clark and guests (editors Chris Palette and Candice Gibson, as transcribed) discuss contagious yawning: its possible link to empathy, theories including dog-teeth-baring and fight-or-flight vigilance, eye cues versus mouth cues in a yawn study, the oxygen-intake theory, and a study of people with autism who responded to eye cues. The episode references the related HowStuffWorks article "Does Contagious Yawning Mean You're Nice?" The episode opens and closes with a sponsor read for a camera.
topics: Does Contagious Yawning Mean You're Nice?

entities.name: Does Contagious Yawning Mean You're Nice?

segments.title: Opening sponsor read and greeting
segments.summary: A short sponsor read for the reinvented 2012 camera opens the episode, followed by the hosts' greeting and introductions.

segments.title: Opening banter and defining empathy
segments.summary: The hosts banter about yawning, with Candice yawning on air. Josh mentions an article on whether contagious yawning means you're nice and defines empathy as relating to and trying to feel what another person feels.

segments.title: Dogs baring teeth and yawning as a signal
segments.summary: The hosts discuss theories that yawning may work like a dog baring its teeth as a defensive or subliminal signal, and mention anecdotes of yawning at dogs, with no study found confirming it.

segments.title: Fight or flight and vigilance theory
segments.summary: Josh and Candice discuss a theory that yawning increases alertness by carrying blood to the brain, so yawning when afraid could spread through a group on the African savannah as a warning.

segments.title: Eye cues study
segments.summary: A researcher tested whether the eyes or the mouth drive contagious yawning. Covering the mouth still produced yawns, while showing only the mouth produced a slightly weaker response, and no yawn reliably triggered everyone. The hosts find the eye-cue idea convincing.

segments.title: Oxygen theory of yawning
segments.summary: The hosts describe the theory that yawning is a way to take in a large amount of air when the body lacks oxygen, and that others may yawn in response to seeing it.

segments.title: Autism study and closing
segments.summary: A study of people with autism, shown only mouths or only eyes, found they responded to eyes and not mouths, which the hosts find interesting given difficulties with nonverbal cues. The hosts point listeners to the related article and sign off with a repeat of the camera ad.
